posts.title: Cleanup Day: Portfolio Goes 3D, GitHub Gets a Real Home
posts.content:
Spent about 4 hours today turning my portfolio from a static page into something I'll actually 
be proud to send recruiters for years to come.

What I did:
- Added a 3D animated background and tilting project cards using Three.js
- Fixed the blog so posts are actually visible to visitors (not just stuck in my own browser)
- Deployed the whole thing live on GitHub Pages at m-m-s-b-s.github.io
- Cleaned up my GitHub profile to look more professional
- Hunted down a stubborn bug where my profile photo kept disappearing — turned out to be a 
  hidden script silently swapping it for a broken backup image on every page load
- Locked down the admin panel with a real password instead of the default one

Biggest lesson: shipping something publicly always surfaces problems you'd never catch testing 
locally. Every browser, every device showed me something different. Debugging that patiently, 
one layer at a time, taught me more about how the web actually works than any tutorial would.

Next up: fixing my project links so they point straight to my repos, and getting a real domain 
name.
